from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Hash Function: The Digital Fingerprint", [
            "SHA-256 creates a unique digital fingerprint.",
            "Data transforms into a fixed-length hash.",
            "The one-way property prevents reversing data."
        ])
        
        # Assets
        input_data = Text("Data: Hello", font_size=36)
        hash_func = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=WHITE)
        hash_func_label = Text("SHA-256", font_size=24)
        output_hash = Text("Hash: 0x5e88...", font_size=36)
        fingerprint_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/fingerprint.svg")
        
        # Apply positioning fixes and assets
        self.place_at_grid(input_data, 'B3', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(hash_func, "C3")
        self.place_at_grid(hash_func_label, 'C4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(output_hash, 'D3', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(fingerprint_icon, "D4", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Write(hash_func), Write(hash_func_label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#3498DB")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        arrow1 = Arrow(input_data.get_bottom(), hash_func.get_top(), buff=0.1)
        arrow2 = Arrow(hash_func.get_bottom(), output_hash.get_top(), buff=0.1)
        self.play(FadeIn(input_data), Create(arrow1), Create(arrow2), FadeIn(output_hash), FadeIn(fingerprint_icon))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#3498DB")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#2ECC71")

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Proof of Work: The Mathematical Puzzle", [
            "Mining is a difficult computational lottery.", 
            "Miners guess a nonce for valid hashes.", 
            "Successful guessing adds a new block."
        ])
        
        # Objects
        puzzle = MathTex(r"\\text{Hash}( \\text{Data} + \\text{Nonce} ) < \\text{Target}", color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(puzzle, "B4", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/computer.svg]
        computer = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/computer.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(computer, "D5", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        # Using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pickaxe.svg]
        pickaxe = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pickaxe.svg")
        
        new_block = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=1.0, color=WHITE)
        new_block_label = Text("New Block", font_size=18)
        new_block_group = VGroup(new_block, new_block_label)
        self.place_at_grid(new_block_group, "E2", scale_factor=0.5)
        new_block_group.set_opacity(0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(puzzle), Write(self.lecture[0]))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#F1C40F"))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(computer), Write(self.lecture[1]))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#F1C40F"))
        # Animate computation process with #F1C40F
        self.play(computer.animate.set_color("#F1C40F"), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Write(self.lecture[2]))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#E74C3C"))
        # Show successful solution finding block creation using pickaxe.svg
        self.play(FadeIn(pickaxe.move_to(new_block_group.get_center()).shift(UP*0.5)))
        self.play(new_block_group.animate.set_opacity(1), run_time=1)
        self.play(new_block.animate.set_color("#E74C3C"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: Chain Integrity", [
            "Blocks link together using previous hashes.",
            "Changing any block breaks the entire chain.",
            "This design ensures total network integrity."
        ])

        # Assets
        chain_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/chain.svg")
        blockchain_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/blockchain.svg")

        # Visuals
        blocks_group = VGroup()
        for i in range(3):
            b = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=1.0, width=0.8, fill_opacity=0.5, color=BLUE)
            blocks_group.add(b)
        
        self.place_in_area(blocks_group, 'B2', 'B4', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#3498DB"))
        self.place_in_area(chain_icon, 'C2', 'C4', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(chain_icon), Create(blocks_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#E74C3C"))
        tamper_icon = blockchain_icon.copy().set_color("#E74C3C")
        self.place_in_area(tamper_icon, 'D3', 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(tamper_icon), blocks_group.animate.set_color("#E74C3C"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#2ECC71"))
        restore_icon = blockchain_icon.copy().set_color("#2ECC71")
        self.place_in_area(restore_icon, 'E3', 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeOut(tamper_icon), FadeIn(restore_icon), blocks_group.animate.set_color("#2ECC71"))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Mathematical Foundations of Bitcoin: Trust through Cryptography
outline.target_audience: University students with a basic interest in computer science

sections.title: Introduction: The Digital Ledger
sections.content: Define the problem of 'Double Spending' in digital currency and introduce the ledger as an immutable sequence of data blocks.
sections.example: Imagine a digital 'magic notebook' where Alice gives Bob a token; everyone in the room must agree that Alice had the token before the transaction is recorded.

sections.title: The Hash Function: The Digital Fingerprint
sections.content: Explain SHA-256 (Secure Hash Algorithm). Focus on the 'one-way' property: it is easy to compute a fingerprint from data, but impossible to recreate data from the fingerprint.
sections.example: Visual: A blender turning a bowl of fruit (data) into a smoothie (hash). You can't turn the smoothie back into the original fruit.

sections.title: Proof of Work: The Mathematical Puzzle
sections.content: Introduce 'Mining' as finding a 'nonce' (number used once) that, when combined with transaction data, results in a hash starting with a specific number of zeros. This requires immense computational trial-and-error.
sections.example: Visual: A digital lottery where 1,000 robots are trying to guess a 6-digit combination. The first one to guess it gets to write the next page in the ledger.

sections.title: Public-Key Cryptography: Digital Signatures
sections.content: Prerequisite: Modulo arithmetic. Explain how users prove ownership using a Private Key (a secret number) and a Public Key (a derived coordinate on an Elliptic Curve).
sections.example: Visual: A 'lock and key' animation where Alice uses her private key to sign a transaction, and the network uses her public key to verify it without ever seeing the secret private key.

sections.title: Synthesis: Chain Integrity
sections.content: Explain how each block contains the hash of the previous block, creating an unbreakable chain. Changing one digit in block 1 changes its hash, breaking the link to all subsequent blocks.
sections.example: Visual: A row of falling dominoes. Each domino is etched with the 'fingerprint' of the one before it. If you move one, the whole sequence collapses and alerts the network.
